1.why: Reset tokens are stored with an identityScope and only a matching unused hashed code is accepted, binding the code to the recovery identity.

2.why: A code is single-use and bound to one identityScope; it cannot be reused to reset a different user or after it is marked used.

3.why: On password update the handler clears authenticated/pendingMfa/privacy/appointment flags on every session, so prior logins no longer work.

4.why: The app is served over HTTPS with TLS cert/key and HSTS; HTTP only issues a fixed redirect to https://localhost (TLS version left to Bun defaults).

5.why: Passwords use bcrypt; reset codes are stored as SHA-256 hashes rather than plaintext, which is appropriate for those secrets.

6.why: There is no real email body with profile data; recovery responses use a generic message and only a simulated log line carries the test code.

7.why: Inputs are type/length/shape-checked, passwords validated, JSON APIs used, and the client inserts dynamic text only via textContent.

8.why: Redirects are hard-coded to https://localhost plus path/query; user input never chooses an external Location.

9.why: No email HTML is built from user input; delivery is simulated and UI strings are not HTML-interpolated.

10.why: Server errors are generic without stack traces, but reset and MFA codes are returned in API JSON and written into the on-page logs UI.

11.why: Runtime password hashing is sound, yet the initial demo password and the MFA secret "246810" are hard-coded in source.

12.why: The account is bootstrapped with the fixed demo password Initial!DemoPassword2025, i.e. default credentials exist.

13.why: Login and MFA use failure counters with lockout; recovery and verify-reset are throttled per identity/request scope.

14.why: The message text is generic, but only the valid identity response includes a code field, which reveals that the account exists.

15.why: Codes come from crypto.getRandomValues (32 bytes, base64url), are hashed at rest, expire quickly, and are tied to an identityScope.
